Only cyclical layoffs during recessions
Zero job turnover in the economy
Frictional and structural unemployment at full employment

explanation: At the natural rate, cyclical unemployment is minimal but normal turnover remains.

distractorExplanations.a: Vacation is not unemployment.
distractorExplanations.b: Cyclical unemployment rises in downturns, not at the natural rate.
distractorExplanations.c: Some turnover persists even in strong labor markets.

prompt: If the Fed raises reserve requirements, member banks must

options.text: Hold a larger fraction of deposits as reserves, reducing funds available to lend
Lend unlimited amounts because reserves are optional
Stop paying interest on all customer deposits immediately
Purchase equities directly from the Treasury

explanation: Higher reserve requirements tie up more deposits and can restrict lending capacity.

distractorExplanations.b: Reserve requirements are binding for member banks.
distractorExplanations.c: Deposit interest is a separate bank pricing decision.
distractorExplanations.d: Banks do not buy Treasury stock for reserve compliance.

prompt: During an aggressive Fed tightening cycle, a yield curve that flattens may indicate

options.text: Long rates must exceed short rates by a fixed statutory margin
Markets expect slower growth or eventual rate cuts further out
Inflation expectations have fallen to zero permanently
The Treasury will stop issuing new bonds

explanation: Flattening can signal expectations that policy will constrain growth or that long rates will fall relative to short rates.

distractorExplanations.a: There is no fixed legal spread between maturities.
distractorExplanations.c: Expectations rarely lock at zero forever.
distractorExplanations.d: Treasury issuance continues independently of curve shape.

prompt: Common stockholders generally have

options.text: Priority over bondholders in bankruptcy
A guaranteed fixed dividend each quarter
No exposure to business performance
Voting rights and residual claim on assets after creditors

explanation: Equity owners participate in upside and bear residual risk after debt claims.

distractorExplanations.a: Bondholders typically rank ahead of stockholders.
distractorExplanations.b: Common dividends are discretionary, not guaranteed.
distractorExplanations.c: Stock values reflect business performance.

prompt: A corporate bondholder is primarily exposed to

options.text: Credit risk and interest-rate risk
Guaranteed principal growth regardless of issuer health
Voting control of the issuer's board
FDIC insurance on the bond's face value

explanation: Bond returns depend on issuer creditworthiness and rate movements.

distractorExplanations.b: Principal is not guaranteed if the issuer defaults.
distractorExplanations.c: Bonds do not confer board voting rights.
distractorExplanations.d: Corporate bonds are not FDIC-insured.

prompt: A limit order to buy stock specifies

options.text: Execution at any price regardless of market
The maximum price the buyer is willing to pay
A minimum sale price for the seller
Cancellation only after one trading day by law

explanation: Buy limit orders execute at the limit price or better (lower).

distractorExplanations.a: Limit orders cap price; they do not accept any price.
distractorExplanations.c: Minimum sale price describes a sell limit.
distractorExplanations.d: Time-in-force rules vary; there is no universal one-day limit.

prompt: A put option gives the holder the right to

options.text: Buy the underlying at any future price
Receive dividends without owning shares
Sell the underlying at the strike price before or at expiration
Convert bonds into common stock

explanation: Puts hedge or profit from declines by locking in a sale price.

distractorExplanations.a: Buying at a set price describes a call option.
distractorExplanations.b: Dividends flow to shareholders, not put holders alone.
distractorExplanations.d: Conversion rights belong to convertible securities.

prompt: Closed-end funds differ from open-end mutual funds because closed-end funds

options.text: Redeem shares daily at NAV with the fund company
Must hold only Treasury bills by regulation
Never use leverage or borrow
Trade on exchanges at prices that can differ from NAV

explanation: Closed-end shares trade among investors; market price may premium/discount NAV.

distractorExplanations.a: Open-end funds redeem at NAV; closed-end funds generally do not.
distractorExplanations.b: Closed-end funds are not restricted to Treasuries only.
distractorExplanations.c: Some closed-end funds may use leverage.

prompt: A convertible bond allows the holder to

options.text: Exchange the bond for a predetermined number of shares
Sell the issuer's assets directly to the public
Reset the coupon rate weekly with the Fed
Insulate the portfolio from all market risk

explanation: Convertible features blend fixed income with equity participation.

distractorExplanations.b: Bondholders do not liquidate issuer assets individually.
distractorExplanations.c: Coupons are contractually set, not Fed-adjusted weekly.
distractorExplanations.d: Convertibles still carry credit and equity risk.

prompt: Inverse ETFs are designed to

options.text: Match long-term buy-and-hold index returns exactly
Deliver the opposite of a benchmark's daily return
Eliminate volatility over multi-year periods
Pay tax-exempt interest like municipals

explanation: Daily reset compounding makes long-horizon inverse ETF paths differ from simple multiples of the index.

distractorExplanations.a: Path dependency prevents exact long-run inverse tracking.
distractorExplanations.c: Volatility remains; inverse products can amplify it.
distractorExplanations.d: ETFs are not municipal interest instruments.

prompt: Junk bonds are characterized by

options.text: U.S. government backing of principal
Zero default risk because of high coupons
Non-investment-grade ratings and higher yield spreads
Exemption from SEC registration always

explanation: Lower-rated issuers pay higher yields to compensate for elevated credit risk.

distractorExplanations.a: Junk bonds are corporate/municipal risk, not U.S. full faith credit.
distractorExplanations.b: Defaults occur in high-yield markets.
distractorExplanations.d: Registration exemptions depend on offering structure, not rating alone.

prompt: A master limited partnership (MLP) primarily operates in

options.text: Retail banking with FDIC-insured deposits
Short-term municipal note issuance only
Federal agency mortgage pooling exclusively
Energy and natural-resource infrastructure with pass-through taxation

explanation: MLPs often own pipelines and pass income to unit holders with unique tax reporting.

distractorExplanations.a: MLPs are not bank deposit vehicles.
distractorExplanations.b: MLPs are equity partnerships, not muni issuers.
distractorExplanations.c: Agency MBS pooling is a separate product structure.

prompt: Structured notes may expose investors to

options.text: Issuer credit risk plus embedded derivative payoff formulas
FDIC insurance up to statutory limits
Guaranteed principal regardless of issuer or formula
Voting rights in the issuing broker-dealer

explanation: Returns depend on linked indexes and the note issuer's creditworthiness.

distractorExplanations.b: Structured notes are unsecured issuer obligations, not bank deposits.
distractorExplanations.c: Principal protection depends on terms and issuer health.
distractorExplanations.d: Notes do not grant corporate governance rights.

prompt: A fixed annuity contract typically provides

options.text: Direct ownership of underlying mutual fund shares in the client's name
Tax-deferred growth and insurer-guaranteed minimum interest or payout terms per contract
SIPC protection on the cash value like a brokerage account
Unlimited withdrawals without surrender charges ever

explanation: Fixed annuities are insurance products with contractual guarantees subject to insurer strength.

distractorExplanations.a: Funds inside annuities are insurer assets, not direct client fund ownership.
distractorExplanations.c: SIPC covers broker-dealer failure, not insurer general account.
distractorExplanations.d: Surrender schedules commonly apply in early years.

prompt: Exchange-traded notes (ETNs) differ from ETFs because ETN holders face

options.text: Daily redemption at NAV from an independent trust of assets
Insurance guarantees from state guaranty funds on the trading price
Unsecured credit exposure to the issuing bank
No tracking of any index or strategy

explanation: ETNs are senior unsecured debt obligations whose value depends on issuer credit and index performance.

distractorExplanations.a: ETNs are notes, not baskets of assets redeemable like open-end funds.
distractorExplanations.b: Guaranty funds cover certain insurance products, not ETN trading losses.
distractorExplanations.d: ETNs are designed to track specified strategies.

prompt: When interest rates rise, an existing bond with a fixed coupon generally

options.text: Rises in price because coupons become more valuable automatically
Keeps the same market price until maturity regardless of rates
Converts to equity at the new market rate
Falls in price because new issues offer higher yields

explanation: Price and yield move inversely for fixed-rate bonds.

distractorExplanations.a: Higher rates make existing lower coupons less attractive, pressuring price.
distractorExplanations.b: Prices adjust continuously in secondary markets.
distractorExplanations.c: Fixed bonds do not auto-convert to stock on rate moves.

prompt: A covered call strategy on stock the client owns involves

options.text: Selling call options to generate premium income while capping upside
Buying puts to eliminate all downside risk permanently
Borrowing to double share count without disclosure
Writing naked calls without owning the underlying

explanation: Covered calls exchange some upside for premium; downside remains except to the extent premium offsets losses.

distractorExplanations.b: Puts hedge downside; covered calls sell calls against long stock.
distractorExplanations.c: Leverage requires suitability and margin compliance.
distractorExplanations.d: Naked calls without stock are uncovered and higher risk.

prompt: Contingent deferred sales charges (CDSC) in mutual funds

options.text: Are paid to the SEC as registration fees
Decline over time and may apply on redemptions within a stated period
Apply only to purchases, never to redemptions
Guarantee the fund's NAV will not fluctuate

explanation: B-share and similar structures often assess declining back-end loads on early redemptions.

distractorExplanations.a: Sales charges go to distributors/issuers, not the SEC.
distractorExplanations.c: CDSC is tied to redemption timing, not purchase.
distractorExplanations.d: NAV still moves with portfolio values.

prompt: When gathering client financial information, an investment adviser should document

options.text: Only the client's favorite stock tickers
Projected market returns guaranteed for the next decade
Other clients' account balances for comparison
Goals, time horizon, financial situation, and risk tolerance

explanation: Suitable advice requires knowing objectives, constraints, and capacity for risk.

distractorExplanations.a: Tickers alone miss goals and constraints.
distractorExplanations.b: Markets cannot be guaranteed.
distractorExplanations.c: Other clients' data is confidential and irrelevant.

prompt: A client's liquidity need refers to

options.text: How quickly assets must be available as cash without major loss
The client's preferred trading platform brand
Long-term appreciation potential only
Tax bracket history from ten years ago only

explanation: Liquidity planning ensures funds are accessible when bills or goals require cash.

distractorExplanations.b: Platforms do not define liquidity need.
distractorExplanations.c: Appreciation is separate from cash availability.
distractorExplanations.d: Historical tax data alone does not set liquidity requirements.

prompt: Time horizon in financial planning is

options.text: The adviser's tenure at the current firm
The expected period before the client needs to use the invested funds
The length of the latest economic expansion only
The settlement cycle for stock trades

explanation: Horizon links portfolio risk to when money will be spent or withdrawn.

distractorExplanations.a: Adviser tenure is unrelated to client horizon.
distractorExplanations.c: Macro cycles are context, not the client's horizon.
distractorExplanations.d: Settlement timing is operational, not planning horizon.

prompt: Risk capacity differs from risk tolerance because capacity reflects

options.text: Emotional comfort with volatility only
The adviser's model portfolio name
Financial ability to absorb losses without derailing goals
Historical index returns in the 1990s

explanation: Capacity is objective (finances); tolerance is subjective (comfort).

distractorExplanations.a: Comfort alone is tolerance, not capacity.
distractorExplanations.b: Model names are not client-specific capacity.
distractorExplanations.d: Past index returns do not measure personal capacity.

prompt: A young professional saving for retirement 30 years away typically has

options.text: No need to consider inflation or taxes ever
A requirement to hold only cash equivalents
Identical constraints to a retiree taking RMDs
A long horizon that may support higher equity allocation if suitable

explanation: Long horizons can allow riding out equity volatility if goals and temperament align.

distractorExplanations.a: Inflation and taxes still matter over decades.
distractorExplanations.b: All-cash may not meet long-term growth needs.
distractorExplanations.c: Retirees face different withdrawal and risk constraints.

prompt: Tax-loss harvesting in a taxable account involves

options.text: Selling securities at a loss to offset gains, subject to wash-sale rules
Realizing gains only to increase current-year taxes
Ignoring cost basis records entirely
Trading identical securities within 30 days without consequence

explanation: Harvesting can manage tax liability but wash-sale rules disallow certain immediate repurchases.

distractorExplanations.b: Harvesting targets losses, not deliberate gain acceleration.
distractorExplanations.c: Basis records are essential for tax reporting.
distractorExplanations.d: Wash-sale rules can defer loss recognition.

prompt: An accredited investor qualification under SEC rules may include

options.text: Passing a state insurance-license exam only
Meeting income or net-worth thresholds defined in Regulation D
Opening any brokerage account with $500
Being referred by an existing client

explanation: Accredited status depends on financial thresholds, certain professional certifications (e.g., Series 7/65/82 in good standing), or institutional status—not insurance licenses or referrals.

distractorExplanations.a: State insurance licenses do not confer accredited status.
distractorExplanations.c: Dollar amounts in accounts may differ from Rule 501 tests.
distractorExplanations.d: Referrals are unrelated to accredited definitions.

prompt: A concentrated stock position may require an adviser to discuss

options.text: Mandatory immediate liquidation regardless of client goals
Ignoring single-stock risk because of past gains
Diversification, tax implications, and liquidity if the client sells
Guaranteeing the issuer will not decline

explanation: Large single-stock exposures create idiosyncratic risk that should be addressed in planning.

distractorExplanations.a: Liquidation must fit goals, taxes, and client consent.
distractorExplanations.b: Past gains do not remove concentration risk.
distractorExplanations.d: No adviser can guarantee issuer performance.

prompt: When a client enters retirement, withdrawal sequencing often prioritizes

options.text: Liquidating Roth assets first regardless of tax impact
Avoiding any cash buffer for living expenses
Maximizing short-term capital gains deliberately
Tax-efficient sourcing from taxable, tax-deferred, and tax-free accounts

explanation: Order of withdrawals can materially affect after-tax income and longevity of assets.

distractorExplanations.a: Roth timing depends on brackets and legacy goals.
distractorExplanations.b: Cash buffers help manage sequence-of-returns risk.
distractorExplanations.c: Deliberate gain maximization is rarely optimal.

prompt: A special needs trust planning discussion should include

options.text: Preserving eligibility for means-tested benefits while funding care
Transferring all assets directly to the beneficiary without structure
Ignoring Medicaid or SSI rules entirely
Using margin loans to fund trust contributions

explanation: Proper trusts can supplement care without disqualifying beneficiaries from vital programs.

distractorExplanations.b: Direct gifts can disrupt benefit eligibility.
distractorExplanations.c: Means-tested rules are central to special needs planning.
distractorExplanations.d: Margin borrowing is unrelated and risky for trust funding.

prompt: Capital gains tax rates for long-term holdings depend on

options.text: The adviser's CRD number
The client's taxable income and filing status under current tax law
The number of trades placed each month only
Whether the security is held in paper certificate form

explanation: Long-term rates follow statutory brackets and income levels.

distractorExplanations.a: CRD identifies registration, not tax rates.
distractorExplanations.c: Trade count alone does not set capital gains rates.
distractorExplanations.d: Certificate form does not change tax characterization.

prompt: An elderly client showing signs of diminished capacity may require the adviser to

options.text: Ignore changes and increase portfolio leverage
Share the client's statements publicly on social media
Involve trusted contacts or legal guidance and document concerns appropriately
Change beneficiaries without authorization

explanation: Advisers should follow firm policy, document, and protect vulnerable clients within legal bounds.

distractorExplanations.a: Leverage increases risk inappropriately for vulnerable clients.
distractorExplanations.b: Privacy rules prohibit public disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: Beneficiary changes require proper authority.

prompt: Monte Carlo simulation in a financial plan is used to

options.text: Guarantee the client will not outlive assets
Replace the need for an investment policy statement
Predict a single certain portfolio return each year
Model a range of outcomes using variable return assumptions

explanation: Simulations illustrate probability of success under uncertainty; they are not guarantees.

distractorExplanations.a: Outcomes remain probabilistic, not guaranteed.
distractorExplanations.b: IPS still governs objectives and constraints.
distractorExplanations.c: Returns vary; simulations show distributions, not one certain number.

prompt: Under the prudent investor rule, a fiduciary generally must

options.text: Diversify investments unless the purpose of the account justifies concentration
Speculate aggressively to maximize short-term trading profits
Delegate all duties without monitoring managers
Ignore risk in favor of highest nominal yield only

explanation: Prudence emphasizes diversification, risk management, and duty of care.

distractorExplanations.b: Speculation conflicts with prudent fiduciary investing.
distractorExplanations.c: Delegation requires ongoing monitoring.
distractorExplanations.d: Yield alone ignores risk and suitability.

prompt: A client with both taxable and IRA assets asks about Roth conversions; the adviser should evaluate

options.text: Converting the entire IRA in one day without analysis
Current and projected tax brackets, conversion amounts, and cash to pay taxes
Assuming conversions never affect Medicare premiums or IRMAA
Ignoring state tax treatment entirely

explanation: Conversions accelerate tax recognition; bracket management and ancillary effects matter.

distractorExplanations.a: Large conversions need tax modeling and cash planning.
distractorExplanations.c: IRMAA and other thresholds may be affected.
distractorExplanations.d: State taxes can materially change conversion economics.

prompt: An investment adviser registered with the SEC must deliver Form ADV Part 2

options.text: Only if the client requests it five years later
Never to existing clients after the first meeting
Only to institutional clients, not individuals
Before or at the time of entering an advisory contract, and annually thereafter

explanation: ADV Part 2 is the brochure describing services, fees, conflicts, and disciplinary history.

distractorExplanations.a: Delivery timing is regulatory, not optional years later.
distractorExplanations.b: Annual delivery continues for ongoing relationships.
distractorExplanations.c: Retail and institutional clients receive required disclosures.

prompt: Material non-public information may not be used to

options.text: Trade securities for personal or client benefit before public disclosure
Support legitimate public research using filed 10-K data
Comply with a client's tax-loss harvesting request
Rebalance a diversified index portfolio per IPS

explanation: Insider trading rules prohibit trading on MNPI.

distractorExplanations.b: Public filings are not MNPI.
distractorExplanations.c: Tax harvesting uses market prices, not MNPI.
distractorExplanations.d: Index rebalancing does not rely on MNPI.

prompt: A code of ethics under the Advisers Act typically requires

options.text: Unlimited personal trading ahead of all client orders
Personal trading reports and pre-clearance policies for access persons
Destruction of trade records after 30 days
Exemption from all conflict disclosure

explanation: Access persons must follow firm policies designed to prevent misuse of client information.

distractorExplanations.a: Trading ahead of clients is front-running and prohibited.
distractorExplanations.c: Books and records must be retained for prescribed periods.
distractorExplanations.d: Conflicts must be disclosed and managed.

prompt: Pay-to-play rules restrict advisers from

options.text: Charging advisory fees disclosed in Form ADV
Using third-party custodians for client assets
Providing advisory services for government entities after certain political contributions
Delivering quarterly performance reports with proper disclosures

explanation: Pay-to-play policies curb quid pro quo influence in winning public pension mandates.

distractorExplanations.a: Disclosed fees are normal business.
distractorExplanations.b: Custody at third parties is standard.
distractorExplanations.d: Performance reporting is permitted with compliance.

prompt: When an adviser has custody of client funds, the adviser generally must

options.text: Commingle client cash with the adviser's operating account freely
Send account statements only if the client asks verbally each month
Avoid notifying clients about custodial arrangements
Use a qualified custodian and undergo an annual surprise examination if applicable

explanation: Custody rules protect client assets through independent custodians and verification.

distractorExplanations.a: Commingling client funds is prohibited.
distractorExplanations.b: Custody rules require regular account statements to clients.
distractorExplanations.c: Clients must be informed about custodial safeguards.

prompt: The anti-fraud provisions of the Advisers Act prohibit

options.text: Material misstatements and omissions in advisory relationships
Disclosing all material conflicts to clients
Maintaining required books and records
Using a qualified custodian when custody exists

explanation: Rule 206 prohibits fraudulent, deceptive, or manipulative conduct.

distractorExplanations.b: Conflict disclosure is required, not prohibited.
distractorExplanations.c: Recordkeeping is mandatory.
distractorExplanations.d: Qualified custodians are required when custody exists.

prompt: Under the marketing rule, hypothetical performance advertising

options.text: May omit limitations if returns look attractive
Must include detailed assumptions and be distributed only to audiences who can evaluate it
Is unrestricted for all retail social media posts
Replaces the need for Form ADV fee disclosure

explanation: Hypotheticals must be fair, not misleading, and appropriately targeted.

distractorExplanations.a: Limitations and assumptions must be clear.
distractorExplanations.c: Retail distribution faces strict conditions.
distractorExplanations.d: ADV fee disclosure remains required.

prompt: An investment adviser acting as a portfolio manager should disclose

options.text: Only the firm's street address
Conflicts only after a client discovers them independently
Soft-dollar benefits, referral arrangements, and any material conflicts
Trading algorithms as proprietary secrets never described

explanation: Form ADV and client agreements must reveal conflicts that could affect advice.

distractorExplanations.a: Address alone is insufficient disclosure.
distractorExplanations.b: Conflicts must be disclosed proactively.
distractorExplanations.d: Material practices affecting clients must be described.

prompt: If an adviser learns a employee may have misappropriated client assets, the adviser should

options.text: Hide the issue to protect firm marketing
Wait until all clients redeem before acting
Transfer the employee to sales without review
Investigate, escalate per policy, and consider notifying custodians, regulators, or law enforcement

explanation: Firms must address theft promptly and meet reporting obligations.

distractorExplanations.a: Concealing theft violates fiduciary and legal duties.
distractorExplanations.b: Delay increases client harm.
distractorExplanations.c: Personnel moves do not substitute for investigation.

prompt: A wrap fee program brochure must describe

options.text: Services covered by the bundled fee and conflicts from bundling trading costs
Only the color scheme of client statements
Guaranteed outperformance versus all benchmarks
The SEC's internal examination schedule

explanation: Wrap programs combine advisory and brokerage costs; disclosure must explain coverage and incentives.

distractorExplanations.b: Cosmetic details are not the regulatory focus.
distractorExplanations.c: Performance cannot be guaranteed.
distractorExplanations.d: Exam schedules are not brochure content.

prompt: When an adviser uses a third-party rating in marketing, the rule generally requires

options.text: Deleting unfavorable footnotes to improve click rates
Disclosure of the date and period of the rating and compensation ties if any
Presenting a decade-old rating as current without context
Implying SEC endorsement of the rating

explanation: Ratings must be fair, current, and not misleading about sponsorship.

distractorExplanations.a: Omitting material context is misleading.
distractorExplanations.c: Stale ratings need dating and context.
distractorExplanations.d: The SEC does not endorse third-party ratings.

prompt: Proxy voting policies for advisers with discretion generally require

options.text: Automatic voting with management on every ballot item
Charging clients an undisclosed fee for each vote cast
Disclosure of how the adviser votes proxies and handles conflicts
Delegating proxy duties to clients without informing them

explanation: Advisers must describe proxy procedures and act in clients' best interests.

distractorExplanations.a: Blind management alignment may not serve clients.
distractorExplanations.b: Undisclosed fees violate disclosure duties.
distractorExplanations.d: Clients must know whether the adviser votes proxies.

prompt: An adviser may not imply guaranteed results unless

options.text: The adviser feels confident about next quarter
A back-tested model showed positive returns
The custodian is a large national bank
No such guarantee may be made; performance is inherently uncertain

explanation: Guaranteeing investment returns is misleading and prohibited.

distractorExplanations.a: Confidence is not a guarantee.
distractorExplanations.b: Back-tests are hypothetical, not promises.
distractorExplanations.c: Custodian size does not guarantee performance.

prompt: Under the custody rule, deducting advisory fees directly from client accounts requires

options.text: Written authorization, proper invoicing, and a custodian that sends statements to clients
Verbal approval once every ten years only
Debiting any amount the adviser chooses without notice
Using the adviser's personal checking account as custodian

explanation: Fee deduction from custodied accounts needs client consent and custodian oversight.

distractorExplanations.b: Authorization must be documented per rule.
distractorExplanations.c: Amounts must match disclosed fee arrangements.
distractorExplanations.d: Personal accounts cannot serve as qualified custodians.

prompt: When allocating limited IPO allocations among clients, an adviser must

options.text: Give all shares to the largest revenue account secretly
Allocate fairly according to disclosed policy without favoritism
Trade personal accounts ahead of client accounts
Promise IPO access in exchange for undisclosed side payments

explanation: Fair allocation policies prevent favoritism and conflicts in scarce offerings.

distractorExplanations.a: Secret favoritism violates fiduciary duty.
distractorExplanations.c: Personal front-running is prohibited.
distractorExplanations.d: Side payments create undisclosed conflicts.
